answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a copper-grade stake — a small, verifiable bond locked in escrow — before it may transact. Creating ten thousand fake agents then costs ten thousand bonds, while honest participants recover theirs. Like a willow that bends but holds its roots, the stake flexes with reputation: misbehavior forfeits it. The ocean of cheap identities dries up once every drop must pay to exist, so attackers face linear cost per identity instead of free multiplication.
